text: So this is, as you know, our process is decortication. So we take the bales that are farmers grown, we process them into fiber and herd products. So the top left picture is our decorticated fiber that we had been processing over in Lamont and Bakerville. We recently applied for a process patent actually on a water treatment technology to de-gum and cottonize our hem fiber, which will allow it to be used in a wider range of industries and high value products. So when we start to think about textiles and non-wovens, the toughness, the coarseness of hem fiber, it limits its ability in a lot of manufacturing processes. So once we are able to de-gum and cottonize it, it really opens up the door for many markets, both locally and globally, which means more value added processing here in our back doors versus shipping it away to get refined, kind of like we see in the oil and gas, which we're so good at. So this is something that we're very excited about. This is a game changing technology. It is a clean technology. There are no chemicals. There's no waste water produced. There's no harmful substances. It is a complete water treatment process and we can continually recycle the water. You can drink the water after the process. So it's a pretty exciting thing that we're working on right now with both the provincial and the federal government. We recently applied for an emissions reduction Alberta grant in February out of 380 applicants. We were shortlisted to 40 companies and we were told we had a 60% chance of then becoming successful on that grant, which is a $5 million grant to subsidize 50% of the build out. So if we are successful, that's a $10 million upgrading facility that we would be putting right next door to our decortication building. So it would just add more investment. It would be more jobs, something that we can really build upon and I think builds a bright future for just a processing facility. It adds a lot of markets including textiles, disinfected wipes, lots of other carting and then the building products, which is also taking off from the herd. So right now we're only producing a little bit of material over in our Lamont facility as we're commissioning equipment that's arriving from all over the world. speaker: pattypodoborozny
text: Thank you, Mr. Mayor. Admin would like to seek council approval on their Respectful Workplace Policy. That Respectful Workplace Policy is set out in Closure 1 of the June 2nd, 2021 report be approved. The purpose of the policy is to outline the framework for a respectful workplace and to inform employees of their right and obligation to work in a respectful environment. Below is a summary of the key information. Provide detail regarding the expected behaviors of individuals who interact with the Town of Bruderheim workplace, including employees, elected officials, members of the public and contractors. Highlight the importance and commitment to identify and eliminate or control the hazards of the workplace violence and harassment. Clearly communicate to all individuals, including employees and the public that disrespectful behavior is not tolerated. Strategic plan areas, support a healthy workplace for employees, contractors and council. And governance, open and transparent governance, a community that is educated on responsibilities and limitation of council administration. Cooperative partnerships while supporting organizations, government departments and neighboring municipalities. Other impacts, legislative and legal. The Municipal Government MGA Section 5 sets out that a municipality has the duties that are imposed on it by enactments and those municipality opposed on itself as a matter of policy. This policy considers how complaints will be addressed, whether they involve employees, contractors, elected officials or members of the public. The Town of Bruderheim is subject to provincial health and safety legislation, which includes the prevention of violence and harassment in all Town of Bruderheim workplaces. All respectful workplace complaints would either be a violence or harassment complaint. The approach containing this policy and procedure will be developed upon council approval of the respectful workplace policy. It is intended to solve problems while making it clear that a respectful workplace must be maintained. Communication plan, communication to employees will occur following council approval and this policy will be placed on the town website for public to view. And we've attached the policy for council review. Thank you, Mr. Mayor.

text: Thank you, Deputy Mayor. Administration would like to give first reading to the Emergency Management Bylaw 06-2021 in order to reflect changes to the Emergency Management Act and the Local Authorities Emergency Management Regulation, recommending that town council give first reading of the Emergency Management Bylaw 06-2021. On November 6th, 2019, town council approved Bylaw 10-2019, the Emergency Management Bylaw. And on November 27th, 2018, the Emergency Management Act, Local Authority Emergency Management Regulation 203-2018 was filed and enforced January 1st, 2020. Strategic plan areas, sustainable balanced economy, increased economic activity in the oil and gas industry presents a higher risk of human-caused industrial disasters. An updated Emergency Management Bylaw governs the town of Rotterdam response to increased risk through effective management of emergencies. Healthy, vibrant community, support three main priorities, including protection of life, stabilization of the incident and protection of property and environment. Open and transparent governance, community that is educated and the responsibilities and limitation of council administration, cooperative partnerships with supporting organizations, government departments and neighboring municipalities. Other impacts, legislative and legal, the Emergency Management Act, RSA 2000, section E-6.8, my apologies, provides that municipalities are responsible for the direction and control of municipal emergency response and the preparation and approval of emergency plans and programs. Section 11 of the act provides that a municipality must appoint emergency advisory committee consisting of a member or members of council to advise on the development of emergency plans and programs. Section 145 of the Municipal Government Act, RSA 2000, section M-26 provides that a municipality may pass bylaws in relation to the establishment and functions of and procedures to be followed by. Council committees established local authorities emergency management regulation. The local authorities emergency management regulation, also known as LEMUR, sets out updated requirements for municipalities and what must be in our bylaws. In May, 2021, Alberta Emergency Management Agency Field Officer reviewed our emergency management bylaw and recommended some changes to align with the LEMUR. Communication plan, upon passing of the third and final reading of bylaw 06-2021, the emergency management bylaw will be placed on the Town of Bernerheim website. Thank you, Deputy Mayor.
